text:
Mavrik Bourque came to Nashville from Dallas after scoring 20 goals for the Stars last season, and the first 18 games have been frustrating. He has no goals on 4.0 expected and 5 assists, playing about 16 minutes a night. He also took a hit from Tomas Hertl on Nov. 13 that Markerzone reported could draw a look from Player Safety.

The drought looks like bad luck. His chance quality, 0.85 expected goals per 60, is right in line with last season's, and his shot is in the 87th percentile. Nashville has also scored 5.5 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. Our numbers flag both as the kind of thing that usually turns.

The five-on-five play is the real worry. The Predators take only 39% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than ten points worse than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a player who scores off the rush and sets up from behind the net, so a new system may take time to fit. His minutes dipped in his last two games; that's what we'd watch.
headline: Mavrik Bourque is still looking for his first Predators goal
